answer: A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases therefore burns capital on every one it does not finish. Because the quill deposit is held in the lantern escrow, the ember audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 77 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. That is 23 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
